   1 | # Post-Incident Review - Data Inconsistency Event
   2 | 
   3 | **Date**: 2025-08-15
   4 | **Severity**: P1
   5 | **Duration**: 2 hours
   6 | 
   7 | ## Issue Summary
   8 | During a network partition between shards, the system accepted writes that were later inconsistent when the partition healed.
   9 | 
  10 | ## Root Cause
  11 | - MongoDB's eventual consistency model during network partitions
  12 | - Write concern set to "acknowledged" instead of "majority"
  13 | - No application-level consistency checks
  14 | 
  15 | ## Impact
  16 | - 3,420 inconsistent records identified
  17 | - Required manual reconciliation
  18 | - Customer trust impacted
  19 | 
  20 | ## Lessons Learned
  21 | 1. Always use write concern "majority" for critical data
  22 | 2. Implement application-level consistency validation
  23 | 3. For financial systems, consider ACID-compliant databases
  24 | 4. Monitor replica set health continuously
  25 | 
  26 | ## Recommendation
  27 | For any system requiring strong consistency (especially financial), MongoDB introduces operational complexity that may outweigh its benefits.
</output>
</tool_result>
